thread:
elaine: Heads-up: sketching a scoring approach for matcher tie resolution. Current behavior is insertion-order and it bites us during canary rollouts.

noah: This is great. Can we make it backward-compatible? i.e., only apply scores when patterns are otherwise equal in precedence today.

kevin: Why not simpler: use a lexicographic tuple (num_static_segments, -num_wildcards, header_count) and compare? avoids magic multipliers and is readable.

elaine: Lexicographic is fine, but we want a single monotonic score we can log/sort and expose in the console. Example draft I used in tests: 

```
score = host_exact*10000 + static_segment_chars*100 + longest_static_prefix_chars + header_anchor_score
```

host_exact is 1/0. header_anchor_score sums weights: exact header -> 30, prefix header -> 10, presence -> 1.

kevin: OK that formula is explicit. My worry: the magic constants (10000, 100) feel brittle. Suggest we document them and add tests asserting no overlap.

riju: FWIW regex-heavy routes will inflate the prefix metrics if we compute "longest_static_prefix" naively. We should measure literal char runs only (ignore regex tokens) to avoid overcounting. Also computing regex specificity is expensive — keep scoring cheap.

elaine: Good catch. Updated rule in my head: compute static runs only, ignore pattern tokens like `(`, `|`, `.*`. We'll include pseudocode in RFC. Perf requirement: score computation must be O(route_length) and precomputed at deploy time.

sam: UX note — console needs to show why a particular route won. I'd like a per-eval breakdown: host: +10000, path: +700, header: +30, tiebreaker: insertion-time. Also when a route loses show the dominant reason (e.g., "lost: header_anchor mismatch"). For rollouts we need a reason code for metrics.

infra-bot: matcher-sim job finished for this branch: 212 routes processed, 17 ambiguous pairs detected. Sample output: https://gist.github.com/redwood/matcher-sim/abcdef (contains pair list and scores).

kevin: Another simple policy: tie-break order = (1) host exact > host wildcard, (2) path static chars desc, (3) header exact count desc, (4) insertion time asc. Deterministic and easy to explain.

elaine: I like the deterministic ordering idea. We'll implement the score for logging and to sort, but expose the tie-break steps in docs. Quick proposal for header weights: exact=30, prefix=10, presence=1. Poll: react with :+1: if that seems fine, :thinking_face: otherwise.

noah: :thumbsup: from me. Please add a perf test that constructs many regex routes to validate compile/traversal cost.

riju: :thinking_face: — add a guardrail: if regex_count_in_domain > 50 warn at deploy and surface it in console. Also add a fast-path that skips heavy regex specificity analysis and uses conservative low score.

sam: UX ask: when a route loses because of header_anchor weight, don't show a generic "lower score" — show "header mismatch (expected X)" so product folks can diagnose.

elaine: Great. I'll draft RFC: will include scoring formula, tie-break lexicographic steps, perf constraints, and console wireframes. Posting link in ~1h. Thanks all for feedback.
